scope.target: Repository-backed design for consistent Python prerequisite diagnostics across supported validator and package entrypoints
constraints: Ask and resolve exactly one owner-decision question at a time.
Explain behavior, compatibility, package, documentation, and test impacts before each decision.
Require Python 3.11 or newer; do not redefine the supported runtime downward.
Apply the approved 25-production-CLI boundary in two ordered batches: 12 portable/downstream entrypoints first, then 13 source-only entrypoints.
Fail before repository mutation or validation success claims.
Do not weaken existing validation, package, upgrade, or release gates.
non_goals: Implement before the accumulated design is explicitly approved.
Silently or implicitly install Python or dependencies; an explicit isolated bootstrap remains an owner decision.
Prepare or publish a framework release.

steps: Inventory all candidate Python entrypoints and classify user-facing support evidence.
Map import timing, mutation potential, package projection, documentation, and tests.
Assess fail-closed, host/versioned/provider runtime discovery, explicit installation, OS-native launcher, and canonical script ownership alternatives.
Present one design decision at a time with impact and alternatives.
Record every owner decision in workflow-plan.md.
Produce an approved implementation boundary and validation matrix.
validation: Repository-native path and reference evidence for every in-scope entrypoint
Valid workflow locator and task artifacts
Explicit owner approval before implementation transition
